summary: A 1934 L-5 cab in Chelan County, in the Wenatchee National Forest; removed or destroyed in 1953, and no source describes what remains today.

facts.status_note: The cab was removed in 1953 (register) or destroyed that year (FireLookout.com, Willhite). No source describes what remains.

visit.trail_note: No source we read describes a route to the site or what remains there.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the cab was removed in 1953. FireLookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed that year. The year agrees across all three, so the story reports both words.
The register and FireLookout.com give 6,834 ft (2,083 m). Willhite gives 6,837 ft. The record keeps 2,083 m, which matches the register.

sources.title: Horton Butte Lookout Site (Former Fire Lookout Sites Register)

notes_for_editor: Three cached pages agree on the 1934 build and the 1953 end. The 1939 Austin Post item and its lightning story come only from Willhite's page; the story Willhite links to was not fetched. One WebSearch found no independent confirmation of the 1934 date or the L-5 cab. A Washington Trails Association page for a Horton Butte hike (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF, Entiat Ranger District) was fetched but not used, because it is not confirmed as the same peak and says nothing about a lookout. Willhite's elevation differs by 3 ft. A 2004 Cascade Lookout PDF on npshistory.com was seen in search results but not read.
